title: Reading notes - LLM inference (papers + conference takeaways)
content:
Quick read + scratchpad from papers / talks (mostly inference-focused). Notes to self and items for Redwood experiments.

1) Flash-style attention + memory/kv cache improvements (paper + implementation notes)
- Main idea: chunked GPU kernels to reduce memory movement + better locality. Big uplift for long sequences + training but also useful for decoding where attention matmuls are expensive.
- Implementation: relies on fused CUDA kernels, careful tiling, and attention dropout handling.
- Takeaway for Redwood: consider benchmarking Flash-like kernels on our most common seq lengths (128/512/2048). Could reduce latency p50 for long chat sessions.
- TODO: spin up a small perf job on dedicated GPUs, compare current kernel vs flash-optimized for 8k seq (ticket INF-4321).

2) KV-cache eviction / partial state serving (paper + talk at NeurIPS 2025)
- Problem: for multi-turn chat, KV cache grows; memory and sharding become tricky. Paper suggests selective eviction + recomputation tradeoffs.
- Notes: they keep recent tokens exact, older tokens compressed or recomputed on demand. There are heuristics based on access frequency.
- Redwood idea: integrate access-frequency based eviction into routing layer. If a request hits an evicted prefix, route to a node with full cache or schedule cheap recompute. Could reduce memory footprint by ~30% on high-turn workloads.

3) Quantization + quality tradeoffs (blog + workshop)
- Several groups show INT4 + outlier-aware quantization can preserve most generation quality for many encoder-decoder and decoder-only models. Quality gap larger on instruction/LLM-eval sets.
- Interesting approach: mixed-precision per-layer + small residual FP16 for outliers.
- Action: test 4-bit quant on our curated open models (gpt-like, mix of sizes). Measure eval set on Redwood Optimize pipeline: latency/cost vs eval drop. Add as experiment to Optimize's recommendation engine.

4) Efficient decoding strategies (semi-autoregressive & speculative decoding)
- Speculative decoding: run a small draft model to propose tokens then validate with big model. Good latency reduction under some network/CPU constraints.
- For Redwood Hosted API, network latency matters less than model compute; but for Dedicated with limited GPUs, speculative could help throughput.
- Quick note: need consistency/rollback semantics in Console/observability when tokens get changed by validation step.

5) Conference takeaways (NeurIPS 2025 sessions attended)
- Strong focus on hardware-aware model design (sparsity, kernel-friendly blocks). Might be easier to adapt smaller open models for production if they use hardware-friendly ops.
- Eval-first deployment: teams presenting continuous evals and canary regressions tied to prompt sets. Matches Redwood Optimize direction.
- Several talks on caching and stateful serving; check slides from session X (Slack thread linked above).

Ideas / experiments to prioritize (short list)
- Benchmark flash-style attention kernels on our dedicated instance types (A100 vs H100) across common seq lengths (INF-4321).
- Prototype KV eviction policy in runtime: simulate long chat traces, measure memory/cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Add INT4 quant profiles to optimize pipeline for 7B/13B models; produce a cost-vs-quality curve for customers.
- Evaluate speculative decoding on a small internal workload: measure p95 latency under concurrency.

Open questions / things to confirm
- How portable are flash kernels across different tensor libraries (triton vs cutlass vs custom)? Risk: vendor lock / maintenance cost.
- For KV eviction, how does it interact with reranking and tool-calling flows where deterministic history is required?
- Quantization regressions: need standardized prompt/eval set; talk to Eval team for integration (cc: Evelyn Park).

Notes to self (choppy):
- run perf job next week on h100-dedicated batch; reuse infra from perf-run-2025-09.
- chat with Noah about integrating eviction metrics into Console dashboards.
- add a short explainer doc for product about speculative decoding tradeoffs (for Solutions Eng).

References / quick links in reading order:
- Flash-ish attention implementation notes (paper): https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135
- Example GH PR for transformer perf (impl notes): https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/12345
- Internal Jira for perf experiment: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321
- Slack thread with NeurIPS highlights: https://app.slack.com/client/T12345/C67890
- Internal Confluence with previous perf runs: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321

End of notes. Short, messy, will refine into a PRD if we decide to run multiple experiments.
